feature: A path drawn with the Pen has a Thickness
summary: Pick a shape you drew with the Pen and Appearance now offers a Thickness right under its colour, exactly where a line keeps one. Before this the weight a path arrived at was the weight it kept for good.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. The Pen and icon frames are on by default.

try.do: Press P, click three spots on the canvas, then press Return.
Press V and click the line you just drew.
Look under Color in Appearance: there is a Thickness reading 4 px.
Drag Thickness up and watch the line thicken under your hand.
Press Command Z once: the whole pull comes back, not one step of it.
Draw a second path, shift click the first one, and read Thickness: it says Mixed, and one pull sets both.
New Frame, pick 24 under Icons, Add Frame, then draw a path on it: Thickness reads 2 px, the weight the frame gave it.

evaluate: Is under the colour row where you went looking for it, or did you expect it somewhere else?
On a 24 pixel frame the useful weights are 1, 2 and 3 and the slider runs to 40. Is that too fiddly to pick a weight with?
The row a path's colour sits on is called Color. On a closed path that sits right under Fill. Does that pair of names tell you which one is the edge?
Should the Pen come back at the weight you last picked, the way a line does, or always start fresh?
Does the line thicken smoothly enough under the drag to judge the weight while you hold it?
rough: The Pen forgets. Set a path to 9 and the next path still comes out at 4, while a line remembers the weight you picked for it. Filed as the-pen-keeps-the-thickness-you-last-chose.

There is no number to type, only a knob to drag, and on an icon frame the whole usable range is the first tenth of the slider. Folded into type-a-number-into-any-effects-slider-not-just-d, which now covers the Appearance sliders too.
The colour row above it is called Color rather than Line, because the app only says Line when everything picked IS a line. Folded into a-path-the-pen-draws-arrives-with-an-edge-you-ca.
